title: An-Nasr: the help
hookLine: when help comes and people enter in crowds, praise and ask forgiveness (Surah 110)
last: AL-MASAD — KIN IS NOT A GUARANTEE.

lines: THE FIRST TEN SECONDS OF WINNING.
cards: A game, an argument, a promotion, a parking spot. Someone wins, and the first ten seconds go somewhere: a fist in the air, a text to the person who doubted them.
Yesterday's surah caught the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ at the start, rejected by his own family on a hill in Mecca. Today's is about the other end, when help came and Mecca opened.
And what it tells him to do with those first ten seconds is a surprise.

teach.h: NASR — THE HELP THAT TURNS IT.
teach.b: Surah one hundred ten, in Pickthall's translation: When Allah's succour and the triumph cometh And thou seest mankind entering the religion of Allah in troops, Then hymn the praises of thy Lord, and seek forgiveness of Him.
Lo! He is ever ready to show mercy. Nasr means help, the kind that turns a struggle.

Commentators connect the surah with the opening of Mecca, when the city that had driven the Prophet out opened to him, and people came to Islam in whole tribes at a time. Now the instruction. Not celebrate.
Not remind them who was right.
Praise your Lord, and ask forgiveness. Why forgiveness, at the moment of victory? Scholars give two answers.
First, success is exactly when a person is most likely to forget where it came from, so you ask forgiveness for whatever pride slipped in. Second, a deeper reading.
Bukhari records that Umar asked the senior companions what the surah meant; some said it was a command to praise at victory, and others said nothing.

teach.h: THE SIGN THAT HIS TIME WAS NEAR.
teach.b: Then he asked the young Ibn Abbas, who said: it's the sign that the Prophet's time is near. His work is finished. Umar said: I know nothing of it except what you know.
The Prophet died not long after. Aisha reports that after this surah came, he would often say in his bowing and prostration: glory be to You, our Lord, and praise; O Allah, forgive me.
And the sirah describes him entering Mecca with his head bowed so low it nearly touched his saddle.

how: Many Muslims say astaghfirullah and subhan Allah after a success, following this surah; the Prophet's words in bowing and prostration after it was revealed are still said by many in their prayers.

o: the help that turns a struggle into victory
a song of praise sung after winning
a victory celebration after a battle

games.q: what's inside the surah — tap the pairs.
p: a sign his time was near

s: the surah tells the Prophet to celebrate the victory
it tells him to praise his Lord and ask forgiveness.
commentators link it to the opening of Mecca
when the city that drove him out opened to him.
Ibn Abbas read it as a sign the Prophet's time was near
Umar said he knew nothing of it but what Ibn Abbas knew (Bukhari).

games.q: Umar asks the senior companions what this surah means. then he turns to the youngest in the room. what does the young Ibn Abbas say?
o: it's a command to fight on
it's the sign that the Prophet's time is near
games.why: the victory meant the work was finished. Umar said he knew nothing of it except what Ibn Abbas knew (Bukhari).

practice: Bring back a recent success, even a small one, and notice who and what helped: people, timing, things you didn't control. If you pray, you can say astaghfirullah, I seek Allah's forgiveness, for any pride that slipped in.
If you don't, simply let a little of the credit go back to where it came from.

wordCard.voice: An-Nasr. The help, the name of Surah one hundred ten: when help and victory come, praise your Lord and ask forgiveness. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: help, support, victory; the first key word of Surah 110.

carryVoice: Your line: win humbly. Head bowed nearly to the saddle, even riding into Mecca. Until tomorrow.
